Rashi on Temurah 4b:10:1.hebrew: לאו שאין בו מעשה - דכשהוא מותירו, לא קעביד שום מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:10:1.english: A prohibition that does not involve an action - For when he leaves [the offering] over, he does not perform any action.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:11:1.hebrew: ורבי יעקב - דאמר לא מן השם הוא זה כו', האי "והנותר ממנו" מאי עביד ליה? הואיל ולא איבעי ליה לדידיה ללאו הניתק לעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:11:1.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov - who said, "It is not from the name that this [exemption derives]," etc. — this [verse] "but that which remains of it" — what does he do with it? [That is,] since he does not need it for himself, [i.e., to teach] that a prohibition that is severed into a positive commandment [is not punished with lashes]:

Rashi on Temurah 4b:12:1.hebrew: לכדתנן - במסכת פסחים, בפ' כיצד צולין (פסחים דף פג.):
Rashi on Temurah 4b:12:1.english: For that which we learned - in tractate Pesachim, in the chapter [entitled] "How Do They Roast" (Pesachim 83a).

Rashi on Temurah 4b:12:2.hebrew: ישרפו בט"ז - ולא בט"ו, דיו"ט הוי, ואין שורפין קדשים ביו"ט:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:12:2.english: They shall be burned on the sixteenth - And not on the fifteenth, for it is a Festival, and one does not burn sacrificial items on a Festival.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:13:1.hebrew: מה טעם אמר קרא והנותר ממנו וגו' בקר שני - דהיינו ט"ז, דהכי משמע קרא: ולא תותירו ממנו עד בקר, דהיינו עד בקר של ט"ו, ואי נותר ממנו עד אידך בקר — באש תשרופו, דהיינו יום ט"ז שהוא חולו של מועד:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:13:1.english: What is the reason? The verse states: "But that which remains of it etc." – a second morning - That is, the sixteenth [of Nisan]. For this is what the verse means: "You shall not leave any of it until the morning," that is, until the morning of the fifteenth; but if some of it remains until the other morning, "you shall burn it with fire" — that is, on the sixteenth day, which is Chol HaMo'ed (the intermediate days of the Festival).

Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:1.english: You shall not do - [The Aramaic "lo ta'avid" means] "Do not do."

Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:2.hebrew: מהני - דמה שעשה עשוי, הואיל ולקי:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:2.english: It is effective - That what he did is done (i.e., valid), since he is flogged.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:3.english: It is not effective - As [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:4.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - והאי דלקי דעבר כו':
Rashi on Temurah 4b:14:4.english: So we read - "And the reason that he is flogged is that he transgressed," etc.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:1:1.hebrew: ומשני אפטורא קאי - ולא קשיא דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא אדרבי יוסי בר' חנינא. וקאתי ר' יוסי בר' חנינא למימר: אף המקדים לקרות שם לתרומה קודם לביכורים, הוי לא תעשה שאין בו מעשה, ואינו לוקה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:1:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: He was speaking about the exemption - And [the statement of] Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Ḥanina does not contradict [the statement of] Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Ḥanina. Rather, Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Ḥanina comes to say: Even one who precedes [the separation of] teruma to the first fruits, by designating the name "teruma" on it before [designating] the first fruits, this is a negative commandment that has no action in it, and he does not receive lashes.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא מימר דלקי - כדקאמרת לעיל: חוץ מנשבע ומימר:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:1.english: And what is different about one who substitutes, that he is flogged - As you said above: "except for one who swears and one who substitutes."

Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:2.hebrew: אילימא משום דבדיבורו - דקאמר "זו תחת זו", עושה מעשה, דמעיקרא חולין והשתא קדש:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:2.english: If we say it is because with his speech - that he says, "This one in place of that one," he performs an action, for initially [the animal] was non-sacred, and now it is consecrated.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:3.hebrew: ה"ג מקדים תרומה לבכורים נמי בדיבורו עושה מעשה - שקורא עליה שם, ומביאה לקדושת תרומה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:2:3.english: So is the text: One who separates teruma before first fruits — also, with his speech he performs an action - For he pronounces a name upon it (i.e., he designates it as teruma) and brings it into the sanctity of teruma.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:3:1.hebrew: לאו שניתק לעשה - לאו דכתיב (שמות כ״ב:כ״ח) מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר, עשה דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:כ״ח) מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו. ודרשי ליה בעלמא, ובהך שמעתא דלקמן (תמורה דף ה:), למעשר שהקדימו בכרי — דעבר על לאו דלא תאחר, שהקדים מעשר לתרומה — ונתקיה ללאוי ממלקות, והעמידו בחוזר ומפריש. ואע"ג דלא סמכי אהדדי, חשיב ליה לאו שניתק לעשה, ואהכי לא לקי:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:3:1.english: A prohibition that is converted into a positive commandment - The prohibition is that which is written (Exodus 22:28): “Your fullness and your tear [i.e., your first produce] you shall not delay.” The positive commandment is that which is written (Numbers 18:28): “Out of all your tithes you shall set apart.” And they expound it this way generally, and in this passage below (Temurah 5b), with regard to tithe that one put ahead of its proper time in the pile — that he transgressed the prohibition of “you shall not delay,” since he put the tithe before the teruma — and [the positive commandment] converted it from a prohibition to exempt it from lashes, and they established it as [a case where] he returns and separates [in the correct order]. And even though they [the prohibition and the positive commandment] are not adjacent to each other, it is considered a prohibition that was converted into a positive commandment, and therefore he does not receive lashes.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:5:1.hebrew: והרי מימר דהוי לאו שניתק לעשה - לאו דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳) לא יחליפנו והוא לאו, ואחריו כתוב עשה, והוא ואם המר ימיר:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:5:1.english: But behold, [the case of] substitution, which is a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment - The prohibition is that which is written (Leviticus 27:10): "He shall not exchange it" [and the positive commandment is]: "and if he shall at all change [animal for animal]":

Rashi on Temurah 4b:6:1.hebrew: תרי לאוי ועשה - הלאוין הם "לא יחליפנו" ו"לא ימיר", ואהכי סופג את הארבעים:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:6:1.english: Two prohibitions and a positive commandment - [The prohibitions are] "He shall not exchange it" and "nor substitute it." And therefore he receives the forty [lashes].

Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:1.hebrew: והרי אונס - הכוונה מאנס בתולה, דהכי כתיב בעניינא (דברים כ״ב:י״ט): לא יוכל לשלחה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:1.english: But there is the case of the rapist - [This refers to] one who rapes a virgin, for so it is written in that passage (Deuteronomy 22:19): "He may not send her away."

Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:2.hebrew: וחד עשה - דכתיב (שם) "ולו תהיה לאשה":
Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:2.english: And one positive mitzvah - As it is written (there): "And she shall be his wife."

Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:3.hebrew: אם ישראל הוא מחזיר - משום דבעמוד והחזר קאי, ואפשר ליה לקיומי תרווייהו, עשה ולא תעשה, דאפשר בחזרה. אבל כהן, דלאו בעמוד והחזר קאי משום דאינו נושא גרושתו, ודאי לוקה משום "לא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו", דלא אתי עשה ועקר לא תעשה, לומר שאין לוקין — דודאי לוקין. וקשיא למאן דאמר דלאו שניתק לעשה אין לוקין:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:7:3.english: If he is an Israelite, he remarries her - Because he is in the position of "stand up and remarry" (i.e., he is able to remarry her), and it is possible for him to fulfill both of them, the positive commandment and the prohibition, since it is possible through remarrying. But a priest, who is not in the position of "stand up and remarry" because he may not marry his divorcée, is certainly flogged on account of "he may not send her away all his days," for a positive commandment does not come and uproot a prohibition, so as to say that one is not flogged — for certainly one is flogged. And this is difficult according to the one who said that for a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment, one is not flogged.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:8:1.hebrew:
ה"ג שאני כהנים דטעמא אחרינא נינהו דרבי בהו קרא קדושה - דכתיב אמור אל הכהנים לנפש לא יטמא, וכיון דחמיר קדושתייהו, החמיר עלייהו טפי מישראל, דלילקי אפי' אלאו שניתק לעשה, אע"ג דישראל לא לקי:
ל"א משני כי פריך והרי מימר, שאני התם דאהכי לוקה משום דהוי מימר לאו ששוה בכל, דכולי עלמא אסירי להמיר. ופריך, והרי אונס כו', דהשתא לא הוי לאו דידיה, דלא יוכל לשלחה, שוה בכל אלא בישראל, שאם ישראל גרשה והדר מצי לקיומי ללאו. אבל כהן שגירש אינו מחזיר, ולא אפשר לקיומי ללאו, ואפילו הכי לקי כהן, דקתני לוקה ואינו מחזיר. ואמאי? נימא כיון דריע לאו דידיה דלא שוה בכל, לא לילקי הך כהן, דליעקריה הך עשה דאלים כולי האי דשוה בכל. ומשני, כהנים טעמא אחרינא נינהו, ואהכי נחמיר בהן דלילקי, אע"ג דלא הוי לאו ששוה בכל. אבל גבי ישראל, דלאו ועשה שוה בכל — כלומר, בכולהו ישראל — דכולן קיימי בעמוד והחזר, הלכך לא לקי, דהוי לאו שניתק לעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:8:1.english:
Here we read: Priests are different, for they are of another reason, as Scripture added holiness for them - As it is written: "Speak to the priests... none shall defile himself for a dead person" (Leviticus 21:1). Since their holiness is stricter, [Scripture] made it stricter for them than for an Israelite, such that [a priest] is flogged even for a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment, even though an Israelite is not flogged.
Another explanation: [The Gemara] answers when it objects, "But what about one who exchanges [an offering]?" It is different there, for he is flogged because exchanging is a prohibition that applies equally to everyone; everyone is forbidden to exchange. And [the Gemara] objects: "But what about one who raped [a woman]?" For now it is not his own prohibition, since he cannot send her away, [the prohibition] applying equally to all only in the case of an Israelite, for if an Israelite divorced her, he can afterward fulfill the prohibition. But a priest who divorced her does not take her back, and it is impossible to fulfill the prohibition, and even so the priest is flogged, as it teaches: he is flogged and does not take her back. And why? Let us say: since his prohibition is weakened, in that it does not apply equally to all, this priest should not be flogged, because this positive commandment, which is so strong that it applies equally to all, should uproot [the flogging]. And [the Gemara] answers: Priests are of another reason, and for this reason we are stricter with them so that they are flogged, even though it is not a prohibition that applies equally to all. But with regard to an Israelite, whose prohibition and positive commandment apply equally to all — that is, to all Israelites, since all of them can stand up and take her back — therefore he is not flogged, because it is a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment.

Rashi on Temurah 4b:9:1.hebrew: ליתן עשה - שנאמר "והנותר ממנו" אחר לא תעשה, והוי לאו שניתק לעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 4b:9:1.english: To place a positive mitzva - [As it is stated], "And that which remains of it" (Exodus 12:10), after the prohibition; and this is a prohibition that is converted into a positive commandment.

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:11:1.hebrew: ורבי יעקב האי והנותר מאי עביד ליה - ואם תאמר: הא איצטריך להורות לנו דין שריפה? ויש לומר: דמן הסמיכות קפריך, למאי הלכתא כתביה הכא סמוך ללאו? אי לאו לנתוקי אתא, ליכתביה במקום אחר:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:11:1.english: And [according to] Rabbi Yaakov, this [verse] "and that which remains" — what does he do with it? - And if you say: But it is needed to teach us the law of burning? One can answer: [The Gemara] is asking from the juxtaposition — for what halakhic purpose did [the Torah] write it here, adjacent to the prohibition? If it did not come to sever [the prohibition from lashes], let it be written in another place:

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:14:1.hebrew: רבא אמר לא מהני מידי - קשה: אם כן, שוחט פסח על החמץ לפסול? ויש לומר דבירושלמי יש קרא להכשיר. וקשה: צרם אוזן בכור ליתסר, ופשיטא לן דאינו אסור אלא מטעם קנס! וי"ל דלא גרע מאילו נפל בו מום מעצמו דשרי. ומזה ניחא למה לא נאסר צרם אוזן מכל שתעבתי לך הרי הוא בבל תאכל, כמו בשר בחלב: דיש לומר דדוקא בשר בחלב נפיק מיניה, הואיל ואפילו נפל ממילא הבשר לתוך החלב אסור; אבל צרם אוזן דממילא מותר, אינו בבל תאכל אפילו נעשה בידים. צ"ע:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:14:1.english: Rava said: It is not effective at all - This is difficult: If so, [what about] one who slaughters a Pesach offering over leavened bread, [intending] to disqualify it? And one can answer that in the Yerushalmi there is a verse [teaching] that it is valid. And it is [also] difficult: [If one] pierced the ear of a firstborn animal, let it be forbidden [as a blemished animal]! Yet it is obvious to us that it is forbidden only on account of a penalty. And one can answer that it is no worse than if a blemish had befallen it on its own, in which case it is permitted. And from this it is understandable why a pierced ear was not forbidden from [the verse] "all that is abhorrent to you" [so that it would fall under] "you shall not eat," like meat and milk. For one can say that specifically with meat and milk [the prohibition] is derived from it, since even if the meat fell into the milk by itself it is forbidden; but a pierced ear, which is permitted when it happens by itself, is not [subject to] "you shall not eat," even if it was done deliberately. This requires further study:

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:4:1.hebrew: וכל לאו הניתק לעשה אין לוקין עליו והרי מימר - וא"ת: וכי תעלה על דעתיה דאביי לומר על לאו הניתק לעשה דלקי? והרי שילוח הקן דמשנה שלימה היא במסכת חולין (דף קמא:), דאם לקח האם על הבנים משלח ואינו לוקה, משום דהוי לאו הניתק לעשה. וכן גבי נותר נמי אמר: בא הכתוב ליתן עשה אחר לא תעשה, לומר שאין לוקין עליו. וכן גבי אונס תנן שאם גירש מחזיר ואינו לוקה. ואור"י דפשיט ליה לאביי בשילוח הקן ונותר ואונס, דסמיכי עשה דידהו אלאו, דלא לקי; אלא שהיה תמיה אלאו דמעשר, דלא סמיך: מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו אלאו דלא תאחר. ומשום הכי פריך: והרי מימר כו'. ואע"ג דסמיך העשה אחר הלאו, מיהו מדמה מילתא למילתא: דכי היכי דגבי תמורה לקי בלאו הניתק לעשה משום דאינו מקיים העשה בידים, ה"נ היה לן למימר מכל מעשרותיכם תרימו, אע"ג דמקיים העשה בידים. מיהו כיון דלא סמיך, לא היה לנו להחזיקו ללאו הניתק לעשה. ואע"ג דוהשיב את הגזילה אשר גזל (ויקרא ה׳:כ״ג) לא סמיך ללאו, מ"מ ניתק גמור הוא, דאי אפשר לעשות השבה אלא לאחר הלאו; אבל מכל מעשרותיכם אפשר לקיימו אפי' אם לא עבר הלאו. ומ"מ מדמה ליה למימר:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:4:1.english: "And any prohibition whose violation can be rectified by a positive mitzva, one is not flogged for it." But there is [the case of] Mimar - If you ask: Could it enter Abaye's mind to say that one is flogged for a prohibition that can be rectified by a positive mitzva? Surely the case of sending away the mother bird is an explicit, complete Mishnah in tractate Chullin (141b): that if one took the mother together with the young, he sends [the mother] away and is not flogged, because it is a prohibition that can be rectified by a positive mitzva. And likewise regarding notar [leftover sacrificial meat] it says: The verse comes to give a positive commandment after a prohibition, to teach that one is not flogged for it. And likewise regarding a rapist we learned that if he divorced [the woman] he must take her back and is not flogged. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that it was obvious to Abaye in the cases of sending away the mother bird, notar, and the rapist, where their positive commandment is juxtaposed to the prohibition, that one is not flogged; rather, he was puzzled about the prohibition of tithes, where the positive commandment is not juxtaposed: "From all your tithes you shall separate" [as a remedy] for the prohibition of "you shall not delay." And therefore he asks: "But there is [the case of] Mimar," etc. And although the positive commandment is juxtaposed after the prohibition [in those cases], nevertheless he draws an analogy from one matter to the other: just as with regard to temura [substitution] one is flogged despite the prohibition being rectifiable by a positive mitzva, because he does not fulfill the positive mitzva with his hands, so too here we should have said "From all your tithes you shall separate," even though he fulfills the positive mitzva with his hands. Nevertheless, since it is not juxtaposed, we should not have regarded it as a prohibition that can be rectified by a positive mitzva. And although "and he shall return the stolen item that he stole" (Leviticus 5:23) is not juxtaposed to the prohibition, it is nonetheless a complete rectification, since returning cannot be done except after the prohibition has been violated; but "from all your tithes" can be fulfilled even if one has not transgressed the prohibition. Nevertheless, he draws an analogy to Mimar.

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:7:1.hebrew: הרי אונס דחד לאו וחד עשה ולא אתי חד עשה ועקר לאו - פירוש: לדידך דאמרת דמכל מעשרותיכם תרימו דלא איירי אלא בהקדמת תרומה למעשר, ואפי' הכי הוי ניתוק להקדמה דבכורים למעשר, אלמא אית לך דלאו שניתק למקצתו אמרי' דניתק כולו. והרי אונס דלאו דידיה ניתק לגבי ישראל, ולא אמרינן דניתק לגבי כהן; אלמא דהיכא דניתק מקצתו, לא ניתק כולו:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:7:1.english: "But there is the case of the rapist, [which involves] one prohibition and one positive mitzva, and one positive mitzva does not come and uproot a prohibition" - Explanation: According to you, who says that "from all your tithes you shall separate [terumah]" is speaking only of giving precedence to terumah before the tithe, and even so, this constitutes a severing [of the prohibition] with respect to giving precedence to first fruits before the tithe — so you hold that with a prohibition that was severed for part of it, we say that it is severed entirely. But [consider] the rapist: his prohibition was severed with respect to an Israelite, and we do not say that it was severed with respect to a priest. Evidently, where it was severed in part, it is not severed entirely:

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:8:1.hebrew: כהנים קאמרת שאני כהנים דרבי רחמנא בהן קדושה יתירתא - פרש"י: ואהכי אחמור דלילקו, אע"ג דהוי לאו שאינו שוה בכל. ולא נהירא. ור"י פירש: כיון שאסר הכתוב גרושה לגבייהו, אינו ניתק הלאו לעשה. דלא דמי להא דלעיל דאמר "תרימו", הוי ניתוק, גם מהקדמה דבכורים דמיניה שמעי' שיכול לתקן; אם עיות והקדים תרומה לבכורים, דכך לי אם הקדים מעשר לתרומה כאילו הקדים תרומה לבכורים:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:8:1.english: "You speak of priests; priests are different, for the Merciful One added extra holiness in them" - Rashi explained: And for this reason their transgressions were made more severe, so that they are flogged, even though it is a prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone. But this is not clear. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak explained: Since the verse forbade a divorced woman to them, the prohibition is not severed into a positive commandment [i.e., it is not treated as rectifiable by one]. For it is not similar to the case mentioned earlier, where [the verse] says "you shall raise up" [terumu], which is a severing [of the prohibition into a positive commandment]. Also, from the [laws of] precedence of the first fruits (bikkurim), from which we learn that one can rectify [the matter]: if he erred and put terumah before bikkurim, [that is rectifiable,] for it is the same to me whether he put tithe before terumah, as if he put terumah before bikkurim.

Tosafot on Temurah 4b:9:1.hebrew: כתנאי - לא קאי אהאי סוגיא דלאו הניתק לעשה, אלא אפלוגתא דלאו שאין בו מעשה:
Tosafot on Temurah 4b:9:1.english: It is like a dispute between tanna'im - [This phrase] does not refer to this discussion of a prohibition that is severed into a positive commandment, but to the dispute concerning a prohibition that involves no action:
